rationale: B wins by a slight margin because it gives the founder one more real reporting path: "The server owners about to find out what their communities are worth," then has the discipline to say, "Without that person this angle does not exist." A is strong, especially "Discord undercuts the 30% app-store cut with a 10% fee on creator subscriptions," but its community angle stays at the safer trend altitude instead of separating the human operator story. This is not a landslide; A has the sharper app-store stacking question, but B is the more useful angle set overall.
gaps_in_A: "Substack's 10%, Patreon's tiers" and "Discord, Patreon, Twitch, Geneva" smuggle in outside platform context the update did not supply. Useful if verified, sloppy if treated as fact.
"Discord servers have historically been free communities" is plausible, but not in the provided facts. Do not decorate the trend angle with folk memory unless you can source it.

"Discord turns 200M users into a payments business" overstates the MAU number. A platform-wide user count is not proof of payments adoption, and A has to clean up its own headline later with that same caveat.
The set leaves the named server-owner story folded inside the trend angle. That is a real separate path, but only if there is a person with community size, pricing, and a quote.
gaps_in_B: "right before an IPO" overstates the fact pattern. The update says Discord is reportedly preparing for an IPO, not that a filing or offering is imminent.
"If the effective rate is 13-15%" invents a range. Ask whether payment processing stacks; do not make up the math in the critique.

"charges for membership in a community ... rather than for an individual creator's content feed" is an interesting distinction, but the update says premium roles and content. Content may still be the product.

The fee angle asks about payment processing but misses A's nastier and more important question: whether Apple or Google in-app purchase fees stack on top of Discord's 10%. That is the first thing a platform-fee reporter will poke.
